title: Virtual nodes and replicas on the ring

kcs.statement: Giving each physical node many virtual nodes (positions on the ring) evens out arc sizes, and lets a larger machine take a bigger share by owning more virtual nodes.
To replicate on a ring, store each key on the next N distinct physical nodes clockwise, skipping virtual nodes that belong to a physical node already chosen.

problem_ideas: Extend a ring so each physical node gets k virtual positions; return the owner for a key
Measure max/min key share across 5 nodes with k=1 vs k=100
Give a node twice the RAM twice as many virtual nodes and verify its share
Write preference_list(key, n) returning n distinct physical nodes clockwise
Edge case: all three next virtual nodes belong to one machine; show the skip
Predict how load from a removed node spreads with 1 vs 100 virtual nodes
